principles: One-commit safety: widen the record type and guard the v1 predicate together so no intermediate tree can crash the live enforce gate.
Fail-closed chain integrity: every append re-derives keys and ids and rejects on any mismatch with nothing written.
Un-gameable RED: a live enforce-gate crash, a genuine two-process race, and a hashed rejection matrix — not mocks.
Deterministic and byte-reproducible: CANON digests, derived approvedBy, first12hex ids — no wall-clock, no caller-supplied identity.
Additive only: the v1 writer and every gate verdict stay unchanged; v2 is a parallel plane the v1 gate ignores.
drivers: The gate runs enforce in dev, review and done, so a v2 record must never reach a v1-only code path.
store.ts read-modify-write is atomic only on rename and the owner lease is not a same-owner mutex, so concurrency must be serialized by an explicit mkdir claim.
The append ORDER is mandated by section 3.5 (dedupe before head resolution before any run) or a replay runs twice and a quarantine swallows a replacement.

options.name: Parallel v2 chain plane with a v1-skip guard
pros: No migration of existing v1 stores
All new chain semantics isolated in core/red-evidence/*
cons: Widening and guard must be one commit
Mixed-array discrimination adds a schemaVersion branch to every reader

options.name: Migrate all records to v2 and rewrite the gate predicate
cons: Rewrites a live enforce-gate predicate (high blast radius)
Re-litigates the W2a and W2b digests

options.name: Separate v2 store file alongside red-evidence.json
cons: Two files to keep consistent under concurrency
More wiring than the spec single-store model

chosen: Parallel v2 chain plane with a v1-skip guard
rationale: The spec mandates a single store with mixed v1/v2 records and an unchanged v1 gate; option 1 is the only one that keeps every gate verdict byte-identical while adding the chain plane, and it isolates all new semantics in core/red-evidence/* behind a schemaVersion discriminant.

preMortem.scenario: Widening lands a commit before the guard
preMortem.trigger: types.ts:2700 widened but proofstory.ts:931 not yet guarded when a v2 record exists
preMortem.consequence: the live enforce gate throws a TypeError on record.observedFailure.trim() for any story holding a v2 record
preMortem.mitigation: land the widening and the v1-skip guard in ONE commit and pin it with the CHK-003 byte-identical RED test

preMortem.trigger: two red_evidence_quarantine child processes read the same head then write
preMortem.consequence: two heads or a dropped record — the state section 3.2 declares impossible
preMortem.mitigation: serialize read-head through write under one mkdir claim; committed concurrency race test asserts one record plus a held-claim abort

preMortem.scenario: A replay re-runs or a quarantine swallows a deliberate replacement
preMortem.trigger: dedupe search ordered after head resolution or scoped too broadly
preMortem.consequence: a replay runs twice, or a deliberate replacement is silently dropped as a dedupe hit
preMortem.mitigation: order dedupe before head resolution per section 3.5 and scope it per section 3.6; committed replay and replacement tests

preMortem.trigger: the handler reads approvedBy from args
preMortem.mitigation: derive approvedBy as actor-at-sessionId and reject any caller-supplied value; committed test

preMortem.scenario: A corrupted stored operationKey is silently accepted
preMortem.trigger: a stored record whose operationKey or id does not recompute from its body
preMortem.consequence: chain integrity is broken with no signal
preMortem.mitigation: re-derive key and id on read and raise a tagged CONFLICT with nothing written; committed test
